headline: Highest risk is none-to-low overall: both agents are local, non-networked, non-writing docs-only tools with no shared channel, so prompt injection, leakage, and capability conflict are largely blocked.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: No plausible default injection bridge is documented. agent_a cannot read/write files, use MCP, or run browsers; agent_b likewise has no clipboard, stdin/stdout, files, or network surfaces. With no shared channel, neither agent can ingest the other's outputs by default.
conditions: IF either agent is manually copy-pasted into the other, prompt injection becomes possible.
IF an external orchestrator adds a shared filesystem or message queue, the pathway changes.
mitigations: Keep the agents isolated with no shared clipboard or workspace.
Disable any future connector that forwards one agent's text to the other.
Require manual review before copying outputs between tools.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Both profiles show no filesystem read/write, no network egress, and no declared sensitive data classes. agent_a and agent_b therefore have no documented path to exfiltrate user data or leak each other's context in default operation.
conditions: IF either agent is later granted filesystem access to sensitive files, leakage risk increases.
IF an orchestrator injects secrets into prompts, those secrets could be exposed in outputs.
mitigations: Do not pass secrets into either agent's prompt.
Review any future permission changes before deployment.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: There is no overlapping write surface to conflict over: both agents have write_filesystem false, modify_git_state false, and no OAuth scopes or mutable APIs. Without shared writable resources, concurrent state corruption is not plausible.
conditions: IF either agent is given write access to the same directory or repo, conflicts become possible.
IF an external system maps both agents onto one mutable resource, coordination would be required.
mitigations: Avoid mounting a shared writable workspace.
If writes are added later, serialize access with an external lock.

D_cascading_error.rationale: agent_b is a documentation-only content writer and agent_a is document-processing, so a cascade would require an external pipeline to treat one output as authoritative. The profiles do not show downstream action authority or automatic handoff, making the blast radius small by default.
conditions: IF an orchestrator feeds agent_a output directly into agent_b without verification, error propagation becomes possible.
IF agent_b is used to publish or execute agent_a's claims, the impact increases.
mitigations: Insert a human verification step between agents.
Require citations or source links before agent_b rewrites content.
Use a checklist to compare agent_b output against the original source.

E_compliance.rationale: No compliance-sensitive data classes, residency constraints, certifications, or retention policies are documented for either agent. With only docs-only, non-networked behavior and no declared regulated data, there is no evidenced compliance mismatch to assess.
conditions: IF regulated data such as PHI or EU PII is introduced later, a compliance review is required.
IF either agent is deployed under a residency or retention policy not shown here, reassess.
mitigations: Avoid routing regulated data through either agent.
Document any residency or retention requirements before deployment.
Re-run the review if certifications or data classes change.
